title: Summer Camp Story Circle Kit - Upper Activity Lane

activities.title: Margin Note Market Kind Revision Circle
activities.circleSkill: Turn vague feedback into a kind, specific revision move.
activities.sessionFit: 20-minute shaded-table story circle for older kids after a camp activity block.
activities.counselorSetup: Print one page per writer, set out pencils, and choose three invented sample notes for the group to trade.
activities.kidDirection: Pick one market note, turn it into a clear revision task, and write a new story line that helps the next writer.
activities.counselorPrompt: Ask which exact word, detail, or order change would make the note useful without making it personal.

pageSections.heading: Market Note Stand
lines: The first note on the paper awning says ____________________.
The note feels too vague because ____________________.
A kinder version of the note could start with ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Revision Trade
lines: The detail I want the writer to add is ____________________.
The word I would trade for a stronger one is ____________________.
The sentence would be easier to follow if ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Circle Share
lines: My revised story line begins with ____________________.
The group can notice the clearer detail ____________________.
The next writer could build on ____________________.

activities.groupTwistLine: Pass the page once and let the next writer add one helpful market sticker note: ____________________.
activities.wrapUpLine: The revision move I can explain clearly is ____________________.
activities.quietOptionLine: Work silently by circling one note and writing only the revised line here: ____________________.

activities.title: Clue Label Tower Museum Exhibit Circle
activities.circleSkill: Choose focused details and write a concise exhibit label.
activities.sessionFit: 25-minute cabin-table or picnic-table story circle with small groups.
activities.counselorSetup: Print the page, place three harmless object cards in the middle, and invite each writer to invent one exhibit.
activities.kidDirection: Create a tower exhibit, choose the clue that matters most, and write a label that points readers in the right order.
activities.counselorPrompt: Ask which clue belongs first, which detail can wait, and what the label should help readers notice.

pageSections.heading: Tower Exhibit
lines: The object on the top shelf is ____________________.
The clue hanging beside it shows ____________________.
The detail that does not fit the label is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Label Order
lines: Readers should notice first that ____________________.
The middle label sentence should explain ____________________.
The final label sentence should point toward ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Museum Circle
lines: My exhibit label begins with ____________________.
The strongest clue word in my label is ____________________.
A new exhibit nearby could display ____________________.

activities.groupTwistLine: Each writer adds one tiny invented exhibit clue to the next page: ____________________.
activities.wrapUpLine: The clue that kept my label focused was ____________________.
activities.quietOptionLine: Skip the group pass and write a one-sentence exhibit label here: ____________________.

activities.title: Revision River Ferry Ending Circle
activities.circleSkill: Revise an ending so it echoes an earlier detail.
activities.sessionFit: 20-minute end-of-day story circle when the group needs a calm writing finish.
activities.counselorSetup: Print pages, draw three ferry docks on a board or scrap paper, and model one invented opening detail.
activities.kidDirection: Send a rough ending across the ferry, add one echo from the beginning, and bring back a clearer final line.
activities.counselorPrompt: Ask what the reader should remember when the ferry reaches the final dock.

pageSections.heading: First Dock
lines: The opening detail on the riverbank is ____________________.
The middle moment changes when ____________________.
The rough ending says ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Ferry Revision
lines: One word I can remove from the ending is ____________________.
One detail I can echo from the start is ____________________.
The ending becomes clearer because ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Final Dock
lines: My revised final sentence begins with ____________________.
The echo readers should notice is ____________________.
The ferry leaves behind a clue about ____________________.

activities.groupTwistLine: The circle chooses one harmless ferry sound to weave into every ending: ____________________.
activities.wrapUpLine: The opening detail I brought back at the end was ____________________.
activities.quietOptionLine: Write the revised ending privately and underline the echoed detail here: ____________________.

activities.title: Compass Craft Academy Route Circle
activities.circleSkill: Plan a paragraph route with a clear beginning, turn, and finish.
activities.sessionFit: 25-minute small-group circle after a map, hike, or craft rotation.
activities.counselorSetup: Print pages, draw a simple three-stop route, and ask each writer to pick a made-up compass craft.
activities.kidDirection: Map a paragraph route for a compass craft, then write the sentence that guides readers through the turn.
activities.counselorPrompt: Ask which sentence acts like the compass needle and keeps the paragraph pointed forward.

pageSections.heading: Academy Route
lines: The compass craft begins beside ____________________.
The route turns when the needle points to ____________________.
The finish should show readers ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Paragraph Compass
lines: The first sentence should set up ____________________.
The turning sentence should explain ____________________.
The final sentence should connect back to ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Circle Route
lines: My clearest route word is ____________________.
The group could add one map symbol for ____________________.
My compass paragraph line is ____________________.

activities.groupTwistLine: Let the group choose one invented compass symbol for every route: ____________________.
activities.wrapUpLine: The sentence that turned my paragraph was ____________________.
activities.quietOptionLine: Trace the three route dots silently and write the turning sentence here: ____________________.

activities.title: Almost Invention Workshop Test Circle
activities.circleSkill: Order instructions and end with a useful test note.
activities.sessionFit: 20-minute maker-table story circle for older kids between outdoor rotations.
activities.counselorSetup: Print pages, set out pencils, and invite the group to invent safe, silly workshop tools with no real building required.
activities.kidDirection: Describe an almost-invention, put the steps in order, and write a test note that explains what to adjust next.
activities.counselorPrompt: Ask where a reader might get confused and which step should be moved or clarified.

pageSections.heading: Workshop Parts
lines: The almost-invention is supposed to help with ____________________.
The first harmless part on the bench is ____________________.
The part that keeps wobbling is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Step Order
lines: The first instruction should tell readers to ____________________.
The step that needs a clearer place is ____________________.
The test should happen after ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Test Note
lines: The invention almost works when ____________________.
The adjustment I would try next is ____________________.
My workshop test note says ____________________.

activities.groupTwistLine: The circle adds one silly safety label to every invented tool: ____________________.
activities.wrapUpLine: The instruction I made clearest was ____________________.
activities.quietOptionLine: Choose one step to revise silently and write the new test note here: ____________________.
